scope: Focused read-only JPEG review; no source edits, builds, production test execution, devices, or screen lifecycle review.

source_checks.checked: All 237 final lines. Huffman construction, entropy completeness, scan block counts, AC bounds, stuffing, restarts, padding, exact EOI, EXIF bounds, and final DQT parsing/reference checks. No additional concrete entropy divergence found.
Frame admission at 196-212 and scanner invocation at 316-317. Dimension/product and encoded/decoded byte limits precede scanning; canonical Base64 is required.
All 249 final lines; entropy parity and matching bounded DQT parsing/reference checks.
Native dimension/orientation, image-count, pixel-decode and completeness checks at 50-83.

Baseline marker layout and eight decoder-invalid case categories, including new missing DQT and zero quantization entry cases. Verified exact mutation bytes. Corresponding Android and Swift fixture tests were read, not run.

other_results: No concrete JPEG bounds or unbounded CPU/memory bug found. Input is capped at 40960 bytes; entropy progress consumes bits, segment progress consumes bytes, tables/components are bounded, and no pixels are allocated by the Kotlin scanner.

EXIF primary-IFD offsets remain unsigned Long values until segment-bounded; entry count and reads are bounded. Primary orientation requires SHORT/count 1/value 1 and rejects duplicate primary orientation tags. Thumbnail/GPS offsets are not followed. No concrete out-of-bounds access found.
No material valid-baseline regression established. This conclusion is source-based, not broad corpus or native decoder verification.
limitations: Parent-reported focused5 success was not independently rerun. Only source inspection, in-memory fixture inspection and an initial narrow Python entropy trace were executed. No builds, native decoder runs, devices, or lifecycle audit. Babysitter run-file creation was omitted to preserve read-only scope; this JSON is the only workspace write by this reviewer.
result: No unresolved concrete findings after source review of the parent DQT fix.

resolved_findings.title: Missing or malformed quantization tables admitted by the entropy-only validator
resolved_findings.resolution: Both validators now retain each SOF quantization selector, parse complete 65-byte DQT definitions with IDs 0..3 and nonzero 8-bit entries, and require the referenced table before scanning its component.
resolved_findings.verification: Source tracing confirms all three original mutations now fail: removing bytes [607,745) fails table existence; setting byte 611 to 0xff fails the DQT header check; setting byte 168 to 3 fails table existence. Offsets refer to decoded bytes of the shared baseline jpeg frame. No production validator execution was performed.
resolved_findings.fixtures: Verified missing quantization tables is exactly the reviewed 708-byte DQT-removal mutation; zero quantization entry differs only at byte 612 (2 becomes 0). Both are included in decoderInvalidCases consumed by existing Android and Swift rejection tests.
resolved_findings.bounds_and_compatibility: Each DQT iteration checks the remaining 64 entries before reading them and advances by 65 bytes. Empty/truncated definitions and invalid precision/IDs fail. Multiple definitions and table redefinitions remain allowed, including DQT after SOF but before the relevant scan. No additional concrete patch defect found.
